title: Feature-envelope applicability gate, pre-registered before any run (appendix W D2 track B)
lock_rule: Criteria and kill lines frozen before the probe ran. Never relaxed afterwards.
why: The Week 13 L3 stage-1 pilot found the most dangerous failure mode in the funnel: EC and PC were scored 23.1 and 17.0 against a truth of 90.5 and 64.9, and not one existing gate fired. The structural SMARTS gates target associating liquids, and EC/PC carry no O-H, so the model was quietly wrong with no flag. This probe builds the missing flag: a candidate whose features leave the envelope of the training domain must be raised, not scored.
question: Given a training domain and a candidate compound, does the candidate sit inside the envelope of the descriptor space the model was fitted on? If not, raise the flag.

inputs.training_domain: probes/l3_stage1_pilot_pool.csv, the 236 known-solvent pool the stage-1 pilot scored against
inputs.note: the pilot held EC and PC out of the training side; the primary check therefore uses the same held-out setting, and the rule must be computable without ever looking at the candidate's own target

rules.definition: per descriptor, on the training domain, the envelope is median +/- k * IQR with k = 1.5. A candidate is flagged if any descriptor falls outside its envelope.

standardise the descriptors on the training domain, then flag a candidate whose Euclidean distance to its nearest training compound exceeds the 95th percentile of the leave-one-out nearest-neighbour distances measured inside the training domain.

primary_criterion: both EC and PC are flagged by at least one rule in the held-out setting of the stage-1 pilot
secondary_criterion: the leave-one-out flag rate over the 236-compound pool is at most 20 percent, so the gate is a gate and not an alarm that always rings
kill_line: EC and PC unflagged by every rule -> the probe is dead and is reported as a failed envelope, not as a near miss. A flag rate above 50 percent is likewise a dead gate.

controls.negative: the leave-one-out sweep over the 236 pool is the false-positive control
controls.rule: the gate is only accepted if it separates the two groups; a gate that rings on everything is worth nothing

action_when_flagged: the candidate is removed from the ranking channel and routed to measurement or a physical estimate. It is never silently ranked.
scaling_note: the pilot pool is 236 known solvents; the real funnel sees a 29.5k candidate pool, where recall is systematically harder. Any recall claim must carry the pool size.

shots_policy.rule: attempts at this gate are counted in reports/decisions_log.md section 12

forbidden: tuning k or the percentile after seeing whether EC and PC are flagged
using the candidate's own target value in the rule
reporting a flag rate only for the cases that were flagged
